rules.title: Service Must Declare Runtime Contract
rules.summary: Every service registered in services.yml must include a runtime_contract block under its local environment, declaring how the service is started, what it depends on, and what group it belongs to.
signals: service entry in services.yml has no runtime_contract under local
runtime_contract missing required fields
interpreter is python-venv but venv_path is not set
working_dir points to a directory that does not exist

rules.title: Health Endpoint Must Follow Platform Schema
rules.summary: Every service with a healthcheck path in services.yml must return a JSON response with status, version, and checks fields conforming to the platform health schema.
signals: healthcheck endpoint returns non-JSON response
response missing status, version, or checks field
status value is not one of healthy, degraded, error
checks values are not one of ok, error, disabled
healthcheck returns 200 when a critical subsystem check is error

rules.title: Service Must Declare Auth Contract
rules.summary: Every service must declare an auth_contract block under its runtime_contract naming the estate-approved auth modes it accepts. The approved mode set is closed (user_oidc, service_rs256, api_key, bearer_legacy); custom modes are not permitted.
signals: service entry in services.yml has no auth_contract under runtime_contract
auth_contract is not a mapping
auth_contract.accepted_modes is empty or not a list
accepted_modes entry is not a mapping, or mode is not a string
accepted_modes entry carries a field the auth-contract schema does not allow
accepted-mode entry names a mode outside the approved set
accepted-mode entry is missing the metadata required by its mode
audience is not a bare app-id matching ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$
jwks_url is not a valid http(s) URL
mode.bearer_legacy entry missing deprecation_close_date or waiver_ref
mode.bearer_legacy deprecation_close_date is malformed
mode.bearer_legacy deprecation_close_date is on or before the evaluator run date
mode.bearer_legacy waiver_ref does not resolve to a waiver_id in output/findings/waivers.json
same mode declared twice in accepted_modes
implementation source code accepts a mode not declared in auth_contract (code-pattern scan)
implementation source code contains no handler for a declared mode (code-pattern scan)
exceptions: OIDC bootstrap paths (/health, /status-app/health, /auth/*, /api/auth/*, /.well-known/*) on services that declare mode.user_oidc

rules.title: Dev/Staging Deploy Must Follow the Canonical Recipe
rules.summary: Every estate service deploys to dev and staging the same way: a Docker container (no bare-metal, DEC-PIM-017) started by an idempotent scripts/deploy-{dev,staging}.sh, fronted by the brokapps cloudflared tunnel and Control Tower SSO, with control-tower services.yml as the single source of truth for port, health path, and auth contract. There is no production tier (Hetzner is staging).
signals: no scripts/deploy-dev.sh or scripts/deploy-staging.sh, or it is not idempotent
a deploy doc or script that describes a host or bare-metal runtime (violates DEC-PIM-017)
published port or health path disagreeing with services.yml
a new public surface not fronted by the brokapps cloudflared tunnel, or not behind CT SSO
a deploy path that stops Colima, the docker daemon, or the VM port-forwarder

rules.title: Estate App Registration Is Nine Touchpoints, Consulted as One
rules.summary: Registering a new app into the estate is a fixed set of nine touchpoints (CT estate-manifest, CT services.yml, CT OAuth client, SCP adoption, ACC estate_repos, estate-dashboard health discovery, doc-manifest, MCP registry, governance docs). Advisory-consult: the lintable parts already fire as SVC-001/002/003 + SCP-R-030; the rest are cross-repo registry entries named here so a new app inherits the checklist instead of reinventing it.
signals: a new estate app missing one of the nine registration touchpoints
an app on a brokapps.ai hostname with no control-tower estate-manifest entry
an HTTP app with no CT services.yml runtime_contract, health path, or auth_contract (see SVC-001/SVC-002/SVC-003)
a hooked repo missing the acc-hook onboarding block (see SCP-R-030)
an app absent from acc/config/estate_repos.yaml or mapp-doc-agent/doc-manifest.json
exceptions: local-only scripts or one-offs with no estate surface (not bound until a trigger)

rules.title: Estate Networking Uses the One Canonical Cloudflared Tunnel Recipe
rules.summary: Every estate app gets its *.brokapps.ai hostname the same way: the dev tunnel brokapps-dev (ingress before the 404 catch-all) and the staging tunnel mapp-staging-hetzner (CNAME to the tunnel UUID). Canonical refs live in control-tower (staging-bring-up runbook + infra/cloudflare-tunnel). SVC-004 covers deploy; SVC-005 fills the networking gap. Advisory-consult: tunnel config is host-side, not in any adopter tree.
signals: an app reached via localhost instead of a brokapps.ai tunnel hostname
a bespoke ingress or a second tunnel instead of brokapps-dev / mapp-staging-hetzner
a dev hostname added after the 404 catch-all rule (never matches)
a staging hostname with no CNAME to the mapp-staging-hetzner tunnel UUID
a deploy that stands the app up on localhost only, never on the tunnel
exceptions: local-only tools with no estate surface
